images.caption:
A wintry morning view over the twin lakes Llynau Mymbyr, at Capel Curig in Eryri (Snowdonia), North Wales.
In the distance, the snow covered mountains are bathed in the morning sun.
Left in pic, the twin peaks of Y Lliwedd, the three peaks to its right are (L to R) Yr Wyddfa (snowdon), Crib Goch and Garnedd Ugain.
Combined, these peaks are commonly referred to as the Snowdon horseshoe.
Copyright status for this Photo is CC-  BY - SA - 4.0.

Credit - Petersrockypics

images.filename: Beddgelert , Cwm Dyli Hydroelectric Power Station - geograph.org.uk - 1711337.jpg
images.caption: Beddgelert : Cwm Dyli Hydroelectric Power Station The water pipes supply Cwm Dyli Hydroelectric Power Station, which was built over 100 years ago by the North Wales Power and Traction Company to supply electricity to the "Portmadoc, Beddgelert and South Snowdon Railway".  The railway failed before the power station was completed, but electricity is still generated for the National Grid.  Yr Wyddfa/Snowdon towers above.

images.filename: Awyrlun o Gastell y Bere yn Hydref 2024 - Aerial image of Welsh castle Castell y Bere near Tywyn, Gwynedd, Wales 50.png
images.caption:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.
Castell y Bere is a Welsh castle in south Gwynedd, Wales. It was one of the most important castles of the princes of Gwynedd in the 13th century. It was built by Llywelyn the Great to keep out the invading English. It is believed that the poet Gruffudd ab yr Ynad Goch composed his famous elegy for Prince Llywelyn ap Gruffudd (Llywelyn II) in Castell y Bere in December 1282 or early 1283.
images.alt:
Castell y Bere, Dyffryn Dysyni, Gwynedd, Wales from the direction of Tywyn.
